title: Pasteli: Chewy-Crisp Honey and Sesame Bars
summary: Toasted sesame seeds bound in honey cooked to the hard-crack stage, pressed into a tin and cut into thick, crunchy bars.
equipment: 20 cm square tin lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Toast the sesame
steps.text: Spread the sesame in the dry frying pan and toast over medium-low heat for 6-8 min, stirring all the time, until light golden and nutty. Tip it into a bowl straight away so it does not keep browning in the hot pan.

steps.title: Boil the honey
steps.text: Warm the honey and salt in the heavy saucepan over medium heat and let it bubble, without stirring, until the thermometer reads 150-155 °C, about 8-10 min. It will foam up and darken slightly. Taking it to this temperature is what makes the bars set crisp instead of staying sticky.

steps.title: Stir in the seeds
steps.text: Take the pan off the heat, add the lemon zest if using, then pour in the warm sesame and stir quickly until every seed is coated in honey.

steps.title: Press into the tin
steps.text: Scrape the mixture into the lined tin, cover with the second sheet of baking paper and press it into an even layer about 1 cm thick with the base of a glass. Take care, as the honey is extremely hot.

steps.title: Cut while warm
steps.text: Leave for 5-10 min until firm but still warm, then lift out on the paper and cut into 16 bars with the sharp knife. If it hardens before you finish, warm it in a 150 °C oven for 2 min.

steps.title: Cool and crisp
steps.text: Let the bars cool completely on the paper. They get crunchier over the next few hours.

tips: A common mistake is stopping below 150 °C; the bars then stay soft and bend.
Use a thick-based pan and moderate heat so the honey does not scorch before it reaches temperature.
Oil the knife lightly for cleaner cuts.
A flower honey such as thyme gives the most traditional flavour.
storage: Store between sheets of baking paper in an airtight tin at room temperature for up to 2 weeks. Keep away from humidity, which makes them sticky.
